standard.title: Evaluate spoken text features
standard.description: Use interaction skills when discussing and presenting ideas and information including evaluations of the features of spoken texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students use interaction skills and awareness of formality when paraphrasing, questioning, clarifying and interrogating ideas (AC9E6LY02). They have not yet focused on evaluating the features of spoken texts as part of their discussion and presentation work — the evaluative dimension is new at Y7.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use interaction skills to discuss and present ideas, evaluating features of spoken texts.

nodes.label: Interaction skills in discussion
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use effective interaction skills when discussing ideas in a range of formal and informal contexts
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in a discussion and demonstrate at least two interaction skills — e.g. speaking clearly, clarifying a comment, rephrasing another's contribution, or supporting an argument with evidence
nodes.typical_width: Use a range of interaction skills across formal and informal contexts — contributing clearly and for an appropriate length, questioning and clarifying others' contributions, adapting language to audience and purpose
wider: Participate in pair, group, class and community speaking and listening situations including debates and presentations, adapting interaction skills to each context
Examine how vocabulary and sentence structure choices change across different audiences and purposes, and discuss how this awareness improves communication

response_modes.reason: Interaction skills are a coordinated set of moves — speaking clearly, listening actively, questioning, clarifying, building on others' ideas — that need to work together in real time. Each skill can be practised discretely but the performance requires their simultaneous coordination. This is the node where components come together in authentic interaction.

success_criteria: Demonstrates at least two interaction skills during a group discussion
Adapts language choices to the audience and context of the discussion

nodes.label: Evaluating features of spoken texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and evaluate the features of spoken texts — including how voice, structure and language choices serve the purpose and audience
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one feature of a spoken text (e.g. pace, tone, vocabulary choice, structure) and explain how it affects the audience's understanding or engagement
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate the features of a spoken text across multiple dimensions — how evidence is selected and presented, how voice features (tone, volume, pitch, pace) support the message, how vocabulary and sentence structures are chosen for the audience — and form and justify an evaluative judgement
wider: Identify key evidence supporting an argument in a discussion between two speakers — evaluate how effectively each speaker uses evidence and interaction moves
Compare the same information presented in formal and informal spoken contexts and evaluate how the language choices affect audience engagement and credibility

response_modes.reason: Students can describe spoken text features (it was fast, it was loud) without evaluating them (and this made the argument more or less effective because...). The reasoning scaffold — what feature, what effect, what evaluative judgement — is what distinguishes description from evaluation and is the core capability this node develops.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Evaluating spoken argument is a rich context — the evidence selection and interaction move analysis connects to critical thinking and media literacy. The comparison of formal and informal presentations gives advancing students genuinely different evaluative material.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one feature of a spoken text
Evaluates the feature's effect on audience understanding or engagement with a reasoned justification
